subject: Velora Systems renewal — tiered rate-lock and burst smoothing proposal
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@velora.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Velora Systems renewal — tiered rate-lock and burst smoothing proposal

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time last week. Based on our conversation and Velora's projected growth pattern, attached is a draft term sheet that blends a committed tier with a short-term burst smoothing policy to help absorb migration spikes. High level: 

- Term: 12 months (option to extend quarterly)
- Commitment tiers: three bands with step-down per-token pricing as committed volume increases
- Tiered rate-lock: committed tokens priced and locked for the first 9 months; months 10–12 can be rebalanced at a fixed uplift if usage exceeds 120% of commitment
- Burst smoothing pool: a shared burst pool billed at a lower overage rate; first quarter includes a temporary burst allowance to ease cutover
- Credit mechanism: unused committed tokens convert to credits that can be applied to burst usage or next-period consumption

Attached: Velora_Rate_Lock_TermSheet_v1.pdf and an anonymized usage breakdown (velora_usage_by_service_Q1-Q4.xlsx).

Two quick asks: can you confirm which billing cadence (monthly vs quarterly invoice) Velora prefers, and whether Finance will need a separate PO flow? If helpful I can propose an alternative with a phased commit (smaller first-3-month commit + step-up).

Happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the term sheet.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Attachments: Velora_Rate_Lock_TermSheet_v1.pdf (application/pdf), velora_usage_by_service_Q1-Q4.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@velora.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-16T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velora Systems renewal — tiered rate-lock and burst smoothing proposal

Karthik,

Thanks for the clear summary and the term sheet. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

1) Burst pool behaviour: can you clarify how burst credits are consumed vs committed tokens? Specifically, we need to understand whether burst consumption always bills at the overage rate or if credits get applied first.
2) First 3 months: we're in a migration window and would like to request a short price hold for the first 3 months (to protect against initial ramp spikes) — would Redwood consider a temporary price-hold or a small discount for that period?
3) Payment terms: finance prefers quarterly invoicing where possible. We may have limits on any large upfront prepay.

Also, can you share whether there are any SLA or latency guarantees tied to committed tiers? Our infra team will ask.

If easier, put together a one-page bulleted summary and we'll run it by Finance and Platform.

Thanks — will loop in Finance if needed.

Samantha Cole
Director of Platform Operations | Velora Systems
samantha.cole@velora.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0192

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-17T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Velora Systems renewal — tiered rate-lock and burst smoothing proposal

Karthik / Monica — quick internal note before we respond to Samantha: 

- On burst pool consumption: let's confirm credits are applied to burst usage first, then bill overage. That will be easier to sell.
- Concession recommendation: offer a 5% temporary price hold (effectively a discount) for months 1–3 of the renewed term plus a 200k-token/month burst allowance for the first quarter to cover migration.
- Billing: support quarterly invoicing. Avoid large upfront prepaid requirements; instead propose a small initial refundable credit (equivalent to 1 month at the lower tier) if Finance asks for some pre-commit visibility.
- SLA note: point them to our Redwood Console SLAs (99.9% per-route latency target) and offer a one-week performance runbook during cutover (ops support).

If you want, I can draft the one-page summary to send to Samantha with the updated term sheet (v2) and DocuSign link.

Laura Bennett
Head of Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
Attachments: none

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cole <samantha.cole@velora.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-23T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Velora Systems renewal — tiered rate-lock and burst smoothing proposal

Hi Samantha — appreciate the quick review. Per our internal alignment (cc'ing Laura and Monica), here is a concise update and an evolving offer we can commit to if Velora is ready to proceed: 

1) Burst pool application: credits tied to the committed tier are applied to burst usage first. Only after credits are exhausted does the lower overage rate apply. This prevents double-billing and keeps cutover costs predictable.
2) Temporary price hold: Redwood will provide a 5% price hold (discount) for months 1–3 of the renewed term.
3) Migration cushion: we'll include a 200k-token/month burst allowance for the first 3 months at no charge; additional burst beyond that is billed at the agreed overage rate.
4) Billing cadence: quarterly invoicing supported. We will avoid a large upfront prepay; instead propose a small refundable onboarding credit equal to one month at the lower-tier rate (applied to the first invoice).
5) SLA and cutover support: we will provide a one-week performance runbook and dedicated onboarding SRE hours (up to 8 hours) during migration.

Attached is an updated term sheet (Velora_Rate_Lock_TermSheet_v2.pdf) and a one-page bullets summary. If that aligns, I'll send the DocuSign envelope (link below) for signatures and loop in Finance to confirm PO flow.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/envelope/XYZ-VEL-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/VEL-2027-RNW-42

Would you like us to schedule a 30-minute call with our SRE and Finance lead to walk through the billing flow and runbook?

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
